conviction_note: Nothing in this file is a sourced, unpriced, company-level number that decides the print. Revenue should land around the $21.3-21.8M consensus, consistent with management's 60%-in-the-second-half shape. The open questions are how the company frames 2026 now that the outlook reads '$85+M pro forma' and includes FanEngine (the Street sits at $78.8M), and an ETH position that has fallen about 22% since quarter end. That gives a slight negative lean (p_up 46). This name sold 4 of its last 5 prints, including a +137% beat-and-reiterate in August (-7.8%) and a quarter in which ETH turned GAAP net income positive (Q3 2025, -12%). abs_move stays at the 13% median reaction for a thin $165k/day name. The findings sum to -0.8 and the scaled number is -1.04; they agree in sign and both are small.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $21.3M (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/game ; Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-08 via https://finviz.com/news/418750/gamesquares-third-quarter-must-show-the-back-half-ramp-wall-street-still-doubts) and $21.8M (ChartMill, per search snippet). These agree within 3%. A single-analyst $23M (StockAlarm) and an outlier $28.3M (Benzinga) are not used. The EPS bar is disputed: -$0.16 (Earnings Whispers) against -$0.12 (ChartMill/TipRanks). FY2026 revenue consensus is $78.8M against a company outlook of $85-90M, reworded on 2026-10-26 to '$85+M pro forma' including FanEngine. FY2027 company guide is >$150M revenue and >$30M adjusted EBITDA (https://www.newswire.com/news/gamesquare-closes-fanengine-transaction). Q3 2025 revenue was $11.3M.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 918,206 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement (1,189,857 on 10-15, 954,962 on 09-30), 12.06 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/game/shortinterest). The page puts this at 7.1% using a stale 12.98M share count. On 18,131,385 shares outstanding after FanEngine (13D, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1714562/000149315226050820/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml) it is about 5.1%. Days to cover is high only because turnover is thin (74.8k shares a day at $2.22 is about $165k/day). This is a moderate short, not a crowded one. No options market, so no skew. The tape is -14.1% over 5 days and -15.5% over 20 days, 54.5% below the 52-week high and 12.6% above the 52-week low, tracking ETH's fall from about $2,690 (Sept 30) to about $2,090 (Nov 10).

findings.finding: ETH rose about 71% in Q3 2026, from roughly $1,570 implied at June 30 (14,840 ETH carried at $23.29M in the Q2 10-Q) to about $2,689 at Sept 30. That makes a Q3 unrealized digital-asset gain on the order of $15-16M, enough to make GAAP net income positive, about +$1/share on roughly 13M weighted shares, against an EPS consensus of -$0.12 to -$0.16. The gain sits below operating income and has no path to the operating guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (release 2025-11-13) also showed GAAP net income from continuing operations of $5.9M driven by crypto, and the stock fell 11.98% (baseline). Q2 2026 carried a $7.8M digital-asset loss and fell 7.8%. The ETH line has not driven the reaction in either direction.
findings.why_not_priced: ETH's quarter is public and the mark-up is mechanical, so mostly priced. What is not priced is how a headline GAAP EPS of roughly +$1 against a -$0.16 consensus reads to screens and algorithms on a thin name at the open. If the market expected that headline to matter, the stock would not have fallen 14% in the week before the print. It did fall, because ETH has since given back about 22%.
findings.independence: ETH Sept 30 close about $2,689 per https://fortune.com/article/price-of-ethereum-09-30-2026/ and the Messari September update (https://messari.io/report/ethereum-september-2026-update). That is a different source for the price; the holding comes from the 10-Q.

findings.finding: Management told the Q2 call (Aug 10) that about 60% of 2026 revenue falls in the second half, with Q4 the largest quarter, and that about 70% of the year's outlook was booked or locked in, against roughly 30% historically. On the $85M low end that implies H2 of about $51M and Q3 of roughly $22-24M, at or slightly above the $21.3-21.8M consensus. Q2 (pre-released June 4 at 'at least $18.5M') printed exactly $18.5M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue +137% to $18.5M, a beat with the guide reiterated: -7.8%. Q4 2025 revenue +142% to $18.5M with the first positive adjusted EBITDA (2026-04-09): +28.2% on 34.6M shares of volume. Revenue beats alone have been sold; the profitability inflection was bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $21.3M sits at the bottom of what management's own H2 shape implies, and the full-year consensus of $78.8M is below the $85M floor. The Street is discounting management, so a Q3 at $23M+ would be an upside surprise against the published bar. If the market believed the bookings comment, the full-year consensus would sit at or above $85M and the stock would not be 54% off its high.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-08, https://finviz.com/news/418750/gamesquares-third-quarter-must-show-the-back-half-ramp-wall-street-still-doubts) repeats the 70%-booked comment and the $78.8M full-year consensus. It reads the same company statements, so it is not independent of management.

findings.finding: The 2026 outlook was reworded on 2026-10-26 from 'revenue $85M to $90M, pro forma for TubeBuddy' (reiterated Aug 10) to a '2026 proforma outlook of $85+ million in revenue and $5+ million in adjusted EBITDA' that FanEngine is now expected to 'contribute to'. The top of the range is gone and a newly acquired business is inside the pro forma. Against $33M of H1 revenue and a $21.3M Q3 consensus, reported 2026 revenue has to find about $31M in Q4 to reach $85M. The Street is at $78.8M. The same release says FanEngine (Peaky Blinders launching Q4) is immediately accretive to adjusted EBITDA and contributes to Q4, and reiterates 2027 at >$150M revenue and >$30M adjusted EBITDA. Net: a likely soft reset of the reported-basis 2026 number, partly offset by a Q4 acquisition contribution and an unchanged 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every 2026 print reiterated $85-90M; the stock moved +28% (Apr), -17% (May) and -7.8% (Aug), so reiteration has not supported the stock. The 2027 guide was introduced 2026-09-09 at a $2.95 share price, and the stock is now $2.22 (-25%), so the market is not paying for the 2027 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The rewording sits in an M&A closing release, not an earnings release, and no aggregator flags it as a guidance change. The FY consensus of $78.8M already sits below $85M, so a formal cut toward the high $70s on a reported basis is partly priced. A cut far below that, or a refusal to bridge pro forma to reported, is not.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.newswire.com/news/gamesquare-holdings-reports-2026-second-quarter-results-with-revenue-up-137-yoy) carries the old '$85M to $90M' wording, the comparison document. The Sept 9 agreement release (https://www.newswire.com/news/gamesquare-enters-definitive-contribution-agreement-to-acquire-sports-music-and) gave no numeric 2026 figure. The positive and negative readings of the Oct 26 release are merged here as one finding.

findings.finding: ETH has fallen from about $2,689 at the Q3 close to about $2,090 on Nov 10 (-22%; -16% in the month to Nov 10). On roughly 14,800 ETH that is about $9M of Q4-to-date mark-down against a market cap of about $40M (18.13M shares at $2.22). The ETH also collateralizes the promissory notes ($12.1M current at June 30; Q1 10-Q terms were 8.5-9.5% with a margin call below 130% collateral). Any treasury-per-share update in the release will show NAV down from quarter end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Balance-sheet ETH value per share was reported in Q3 2025 ($0.83/share pre-split) and Q2 2026 ($0.25/share pre-split). Both prints fell (-12%, -7.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -14% over 5 days, which tracks ETH. What is left is a margin-call or treasury-sale disclosure (sales funded buybacks in H1) that the market cannot see until the release. Had the market priced a forced sale, the stock would trade below its ETH-net-of-notes value, and it does not appear to.
findings.independence: Holdings and note terms: Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1714562/000149315226037832/form10-q.htm and CryptoSlate on cash versus ETH (https://cryptoslate.com/gaming-firm-gamesquare-boasts-a-26m-ethereum-fortune-but-quiet-debt-fine-print-leaves-just-2-1m-in-real-cash/). The ETH price series is independent of the company.

findings.finding: The company pre-announced Q2 revenue mid-quarter, in a June 4 shareholder letter saying 'at least $18.5M' (8-K 7.01), during a proxy campaign. It has issued no Q3 preliminary despite holding a special meeting on Oct 22 and putting out several releases since quarter end (Oct 26 closing, Nov 2 date, Nov 5 Hatchet, Nov 12 Peaky Blinders). None of them gave a Q3 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the June pre-release, the Q2 print itself fell 7.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from absence, and the June letter had a proxy-vote motive that the October vote (on FanEngine) shared. It is weak, and it is sized as weak.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001714562.json): no 8-K item 2.02 or 7.01 with Q3 numbers between Sept 30 and Nov 13. The Oct 26 8-K 7.01 covers only the closing. That is a different document; the inference is the same.

findings.finding: FanEngine closed Oct 26 for 5,439,416 new shares, 30% of the 18.13M post-closing count. Form D values them at $12,565,051, about $2.31/share, against a $2.22 spot. Up to 1.41M earnout shares and $50M cash earnouts follow. Q3 per-share figures use the pre-deal count, and Q4 onward is diluted about 42%. The shares are unregistered (Item 3.02), so there is no resale overhang inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print followed an issuance of this size. The stock fell from $2.95 (deal announcement price, Sept 4) to $2.22.
findings.why_not_priced: The dilution is public and mostly priced. The new per-share treasury and EPS math appears in an earnings release for the first time on Nov 16, and estimate pages still carry the 12.98M share count (equibles), so per-share figures may surprise screens.
findings.independence: 8-K 2.01/3.02 of 2026-10-26 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1714562/000149315226048423/form8-k.htm) and the Goff and Blue & Silver 13D/As showing dilution below 5%. All of these are company-side documents.

findings.finding: Short interest was 918k shares at the 10-30 settlement (down from 1.19M on 10-15), about 5.1% of the 18.13M post-deal shares, with 12 days to cover because daily volume is about 75k shares. A thin float with double-digit days to cover gives a mechanical squeeze path on a good headline. The Q4 2025 print moved +28% on 34.6M shares, 450x normal volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-09: +28.17% on 34.6M shares against a 76k median. The volume path for a squeeze exists in this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set; this is a mechanism, not news. It is sized small and filed for the panel.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The small negative lean agrees with the -15% 20-day run-up and this name's habit of selling prints. The free control (-run_up) would argue for a bounce, and the stock now trades near its ETH value net of notes, which is why p_up is only 4 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): revenue-in-line finding cut +1.0 to +0.5 because this name sold the Aug beat (-7.8%) and 4 of its last 5 prints.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): ETH Q3 mark-up gain cut +0.5 to +0.3; the Q3 2025 analogue (GAAP profit on crypto) fell 12%.

Two readings of one document are one finding: the Oct 26 guidance rewording (-1.5) and the FanEngine/Peaky Blinders Q4 contribution (+0.5) both came from the closing release, so they are merged into one guidance finding at -0.8 after also shrinking for lesson 7.
Lesson 5 (proxy, priced, absence): ETH post-quarter decline cut -1.0 to -0.6 because the tape already tracks ETH. The no-preannouncement inference was cut -0.5 to -0.2 as an inference from absence.

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked (about 5% of post-deal shares, 12 DTC on thin volume). The positioning finding is kept at +0.3; negatives are trimmed slightly. p_up moved 47 to 46 after the merged guidance read, which leaves a net negative bias on the reported basis.
Lesson 6 (bar): revenue bar sourced to two agreeing estimates. The EPS bar is disputed, so the ETH/EPS finding stays capped small.
